citations.anchor: refuses to demote the last remaining admin with 409
citations.why: PATCHing the sole active admin down to viewer is answered 409 and the role is asserted unchanged, so the last admin cannot be demoted.

citations.anchor: refuses to disable the only active admin with 409
citations.why: Disabling the sole active admin is answered 409 and the account is asserted still active, pinning the other half of the guard.

citations.anchor: leaves one admin standing when two demotions race
citations.why: Two concurrent demotions of the last two admins end with exactly one admin left, which only holds if the count is read under the lock rather than count-then-write.

citations.anchor: loads under the admin lock and reads the count after it
citations.why: Asserts the ordering the invariant names: the aggregate is loaded with the global active-admin lock taken and the counter is read after it.

citations.anchor: refuses to let a member disable themselves with 409
citations.why: An admin disabling their own id gets 409 and stays active.

citations.anchor: tags a self role change as SELF_ACTION
citations.why: PATCHing your own role is refused with 409/SELF_ACTION.

citations.anchor: lets a member rename themselves
citations.why: Pins the positive clause: a self-PATCH that only changes name succeeds and persists.

citations.anchor: sessions inside the transaction, after the save
citations.why: Asserts the session revoke is invoked inside the unit of work and after the aggregate save, so the two cannot commit separately.

citations.anchor: propagates a failing revoke out of the unit of work
citations.why: A throwing session revoker aborts the whole unit of work, ruling out the 'disabled but sessions alive' state.

citations.anchor: leaves no usable credential behind, whichever side wins
citations.why: End-to-end: a login racing a disable never leaves a live session on a disabled account, whichever order the two commit in.

citations.anchor: rotates the invite token, keeping exactly one live
citations.why: After a resend the invite-token rows for the user are asserted to number exactly one, and to be a different hash.

citations.anchor: keeps one live token when two resends race
citations.why: Two concurrent resends leave exactly one token row, which is the per-user lock doing its job.

citations.anchor: takes the advisory lock before touching any row
citations.why: Asserts the delete+insert pair happens after the per-user advisory lock is taken.

citations.anchor: takes the advisory lock before touching any row
citations.why: Same assertion for the reset token, pinning the 'at most one reset token' half.

citations.anchor: stores only the SHA-256, and returns the raw token exactly once
citations.why: The stored row carries only the hash and the raw token is handed back once by the rotate call.

citations.anchor: stores only the SHA-256, and returns the raw token exactly once
citations.why: Same for the reset token.

citations.anchor: returns the paginated envelope with the expected shape
citations.why: Asserts the exact key set of a member in the list read, so a raw token appearing on that read would fail it; the 'exactly three routes' enumeration is not itself pinned anywhere.

citations.anchor: hands the raw token back exactly once, on invite
citations.why: The invite response carries the raw token and the subsequent reads of that invite do not.

citations.anchor: refuses a resend issued moments ago, with a machine code
citations.why: A resend inside the window is 409 with code INVITE_RECENTLY_SENT and a retryAfterSeconds bounded by 60, and the existing token is untouched.

citations.anchor: refuses a rotation inside the cooldown, having already taken the lock
citations.why: Pins that the cooldown check runs after the advisory lock is taken, i.e. inside the same lock as the rotation.

citations.anchor: refuses an issue inside the cooldown, having already taken the lock
citations.why: Same ordering for the password-reset rotation.

citations.anchor: revokes a pending invite, deleting the placeholder user (204)
citations.why: The pending row is the one the route deletes, asserted gone from the users table.

citations.anchor: refuses to revoke an active member with 409
citations.why: A real account is refused, pinning 'a real account is never deleted' for the active case.

citations.anchor: rejects revoking a non-pending member
citations.why: The aggregate refuses revokeInvite for every non-pending status, covering disabled as well as active.

citations.anchor: rejects a pending member — there is no password to reset yet
citations.why: ensureCanResetPassword throws for pending; the HTTP status for this path is only pinned generically by conflict.spec, not end to end.

citations.anchor: rejects a disabled member — a reset must not reopen a closed account
citations.why: ensureCanResetPassword throws for disabled.

citations.anchor: returns the raw token for an active member
citations.why: Pins the positive half: only the active member gets a link minted.

citations.anchor: rejects resending to an active member with 409
citations.why: Resend is refused for a non-pending member.

citations.anchor: rejects disabling an already-disabled member with 409
citations.why: Disable is refused for a non-active member.

citations.anchor: rejects enabling an already-active member with 409
citations.why: Enable is refused for an active member.

citations.anchor: rejects enabling a pending member with 409
citations.why: Enable is refused for a pending member, completing 're-enabling only for disabled'.

citations.anchor: refuses a second row differing only in case
citations.why: Inserts directly into the users table, bypassing every application check, and asserts the database itself raises a duplicate-key error — which is the invariant's point that the guarantee is the lower(email) index.

citations.anchor: treats an existing email case-insensitively (409)
citations.why: Inviting a differently-cased duplicate through the route is a 409.

citations.anchor: lets only one of two concurrent invites to one address through
citations.why: Two concurrent invites to one address leave exactly one row, which no in-code check could guarantee.

citations.anchor: rejects a whitespace-only name — trimmed first, so isNotEmpty sees it
citations.why: The invite DTO trims before validating, so a spaces-only name fails validation.

citations.anchor: rejects a whitespace-only name — trimmed first, so isNotEmpty sees it
citations.why: The patch DTO does the same, pinning the 'both DTOs' clause.

citations.anchor: binds OriginGuard when it has a state-changing handler
citations.why: Iterates every controller the module mounts and asserts OriginGuard is bound exactly when the controller has a non-GET handler.

citations.anchor: binds PermissionsGuard
citations.why: Every mounted controller is asserted to bind PermissionsGuard.

citations.anchor: requires a permission from the shared catalogue
citations.why: Every controller declares at least one permission and each one is a member of the shared PERMISSIONS catalogue, pinning 'with a permission constant'.

citations.anchor: exposes no public route
citations.why: No controller or handler carries @Public(), pinning 'the package has no public routes'.

citations.anchor: ships no migrations — it owns no schema
citations.why: Pins the first clause off the plugin descriptor; the second clause (every write lands in an identity- or workspaces-migrated table) is not asserted anywhere.

citations.anchor: appends both facts when a patch changes name and role
citations.why: A patch touching both fields appends exactly the two corresponding events, no more.

citations.anchor: writes nothing when the patch changes neither
citations.why: A no-op patch appends nothing, pinning 'every state change' against spurious events.

citations.anchor: stamps the actor on every appended event
citations.why: Pins the 'with the actor attached' clause.

citations.anchor: appends inside the unit of work, not after it
citations.why: Pins the 'in the same transaction as the write' clause.

citations.anchor: own member.disabled fact
citations.why: The disable path drains exactly the aggregate's member.disabled event into the outbox.

citations.anchor: imports nothing from %s
citations.why: Reads every non-spec file under domain/ and asserts none imports @nestjs/*, drizzle-orm, class-validator, or anything under infrastructure — exactly the four prohibitions.

citations.anchor: Disable inert, with the reason on it
citations.why: The flag's only effect is on the control: the row menu's Disable is aria-disabled with the reason, and a forced click sends no request.

citations.anchor: locks the sole active admin with the reason
citations.why: The Role tab's Apply button is disabled with the reason when the flag is set, again a control-state effect only.

citations.anchor: refuses to disable the only active admin with 409
citations.why: The server refuses the request on its own recount, with no client flag in the payload — so a stale or wrong isLastAdmin cannot produce a violation of I-01.

citations.anchor: reads the workspace from the run context
citations.why: The handler queries with the run context's workspace id.

citations.anchor: ignores a workspaceId smuggled into the arguments
citations.why: A workspaceId in the tool arguments is not read, so the answer stays scoped to the run's workspace; the 'returns neither tokens nor session data' clause is not asserted anywhere — nothing pins the tool's output shape.

citations.anchor: exports nothing and is not global
citations.why: Asserts forRoot() returns a module with no exports and global falsy, so no provider is visible to neighbours.
